title: The green that was almost right
scenario:
A stationery brand launches a notebook line. Its brand book has two colours. Your teammate set up drafts on three image tools and wrote down what happened.

Use the exhibit. The brand, the requests and the notes are made up for this case. The field names are from the vendors' docs in October 2026.

questions.prompt: Draft 1 put the green on the desk, not the cover. Which rewrite fits BFL's hex guide best?

options.text: A notebook on a desk, use #2E6B4F and #C4725A as much as you can
options.explanation: The codes are still not tied to objects. The BFL docs warn that vague references may give inconsistent results.

options.text: A notebook with a cover in color #2E6B4F and a band in color #C4725A
options.explanation: Right. The BFL docs say to associate each code with an object or surface, such as "the mug in color #FF0000".

options.text: A notebook on a desk, brand colours #2E6B4F, #C4725A, very important
options.explanation: Stressing the codes does not say where each colour goes. Each code needs its own object.

options.text: A notebook on a desk in forest green and terracotta, with no codes
options.explanation: Words alone name a family of colours, not the brand's exact colours. This drops the codes.

questions.prompt: Draft 2: what is wrong with the Ideogram palette list?

options.text: It has too many colours for one image's palette in a JSON prompt
options.explanation: Ideogram allows up to 16 colours for the whole image. Two is well under that.

options.text: Palette colours must go on each element, never on the whole image
options.explanation: Ideogram has both: style_description.color_palette for the image and color_palette per element.

options.text: The codes must be uppercase and in full: #2E6B4F and #C4725A
options.explanation: Right. The Ideogram docs say to write hex codes in uppercase #RRGGBB, never #rgb or lowercase.

options.text: Hex codes do not work in Ideogram 4.5; use colour words instead
options.explanation: Ideogram 4.5 and 4.0 accept hex colours in a JSON prompt's color_palette.

questions.prompt: Draft 3 breaks one of the rules on Recraft's colors list. Which change fixes it?

options.text: Change the weights so that together they add up to 1.0 or less
options.explanation: Right. The Recraft docs say weights are set for every colour or none, and their sum must not exceed 1.0. Here 0.7 + 0.5 = 1.2.

options.text: Replace each rgb list with the hex code written as a plain string
options.explanation: Recraft's colour object has a required rgb field of three integers from 0 to 255.

options.text: Remove the weight from only the second colour and keep the first
options.explanation: The Recraft docs say weights must be set either for every colour or for none.

options.text: Add eight more colours so the palette has the full ten colours
options.explanation: Ten is the maximum, not a minimum. The problem is the weights.

questions.prompt: The client wants a promise that the cover will be exactly #2E6B4F. What is your honest answer?

options.text: Yes: once the hex code is in the prompt, the model matches it exactly
options.explanation: The BFL docs say to check the rendered colour when accuracy matters. A code in the prompt is not a promise.

options.text: Yes, if we use Ideogram's palette, because it locks every pixel
options.explanation: The Ideogram docs say Ideogram's palettes steer the colours strongly but don't lock every pixel.

options.text: No: codes steer the colour; we check it with a picker and fix by hand
options.explanation: Right. Each vendor hedges: the BFL docs say check the rendered colour, the Ideogram docs say it doesn't lock every pixel, the Recraft docs say preferable colours.

options.text: No: image models cannot take colour codes, so we pick colours later
options.explanation: BFL, Ideogram and Recraft all take colour codes. They steer the colour; they don't guarantee it.
